summaryBox.title: The Halogen Anomaly Rule
summaryBox.takeaway: Halogens are Ortho/Para-directing (+M) but DEACTIVATING (-I > +M). Chlorobenzene reacts slower than benzene.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ELECTROPHILIC SUBSTITUTION ON CHLOROBENZENE
                       
   Chlorination:   $\text{Ph-Cl} + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Anhyd. FeCl}_3} \text{1,4-Dichlorobenzene (Major, } p\text{-}) + \text{1,2-Dichlorobenzene (Minor, } o\text{-})$
   Nitration:      $\text{Ph-Cl} + \text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene (Major)}} + \text{1-Chloro-2-nitrobenzene}$
   Sulfonation:    $\text{Ph-Cl} + \text{Fuming H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{4-Chlorobenzenesulfonic acid (Major)}}$
   FC Alkylation:  $\text{Ph-Cl} + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}/\text{AlCl}_3 \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{1-Chloro-4-methylbenzene (Major)}}$
conceptBreakdown.content:
Halogens on a benzene ring exert two opposing electronic effects:
1. **Strong -I Effect**: Withdraws $\sigma$-electron density, overall deactivating the ring ($r_{\text{PhX}} < r_{\text{benzene}}$).
2. **Weak +M Effect**: Donates p-electrons into the ring via resonance, specifically stabilizing *ortho* and *para* arenium carbocation intermediates.
$$\mathbf{\text{Halogens are Ortho/Para-Directing BUT DEACTIVATING!}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Landmark S_EAr Reactions of Chlorobenzene
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Landmark S_EAr Reactions of Chlorobenzene
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
S_EAr REACTIONS OF CHLOROBENZENE:

• Chlorination: Ph-Cl + Cl₂ / FeCl₃ ──► 1,4-Dichlorobenzene (Major, p-) + 1,2-Dichlorobenzene (Minor, o-)
• Nitration:    Ph-Cl + HNO₃ / H₂SO₄ ──► 1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene (Major, p-)
• Sulfonation:  Ph-Cl + H₂SO₄ (fuming) ──► 4-Chlorobenzenesulfonic acid (Major, p-)
• FC Alkylation: Ph-Cl + CH₃Cl / AlCl₃ ──► 1-Chloro-4-methylbenzene (Major, p-)
conceptBreakdown.content: In all electrophilic substitutions, the *para*-isomer is the major product due to minimal steric repulsion between the chlorine atom and the incoming electrophile.

quickRevision: Chlorobenzene reacts slower than benzene in S_EAr.
Para isomer is the major product due to minimal steric hindrance.
